{"cloudId":"c08225c2-3ed9-4a44-8526-4f5589f2b403","projectKey":"TLCSDIS","issueTypeName":"Story","summary":"TE Architecture Design — MoE & Flash Attention Research and Experiment Planning","description":"## Objective
Establish the architectural blueprint and experimentation methodology for enhancing the hierarchical clinical transformer with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) and Flash Attention, enabling faster training and improved patient subpopulation specialization.

## Acceptance Criteria
- MoE integration strategy defined with placement rationale (layers 2-5 of temporal encoder)
- Flash Attention analysis complete with expected performance gains quantified
- 6-experiment ablation study designed with controlled variables and computational equivalence
- Output strategy evaluated and decision made (standard softmax with 8.1K target codes)
- Healthcare-optimized evaluation metrics defined (Top-K Accuracy, MRR, Stratified Performance)
- Complete implementation code produced for both Flash Attention and MoE frameworks

## Background
The hierarchical clinical transformer processes 200-day patient sequences with 80 codes per day across 84K input vocabulary. This stage focused on designing architectural enhancements grounded in literature (Switch Transformer, Mixtral, DeepSeek-V3) adapted to healthcare domain characteristics.

## Technical Details
- **MoE Design**: 8 experts (matching ~8 patient archetypes), top-2 routing, layers 2-5, shared expert variant
- **Flash Attention**: O(N) memory via PyTorch 2.0+ SDPA, expected 3x speedup, 12.5x attention memory reduction
- **Load Balancing**: Switch auxiliary loss + DeepSeek bias correction (auxiliary-loss-free) both designed
- **Ablation Study**: 6 experiments (Dense baseline, Standard MoE, Shared Expert, Fine-Grained 16E, Auxiliary-Free, Next-Day Prediction)
- **Output**: 7,242 lines of documentation and implementation code produced

## Key Decisions
1. Flash Attention as foundation for ALL experiments (enables 4x batch size, cleaner comparison)
2. 8 experts at layers 2-5 as "Goldilocks zone" (85% confidence)
3. Top-K=2 routing (90% confidence, matches multi-morbidity patterns)
4. Healthcare metrics over perplexity (Top-K, MRR, Stratified as primary)
5. Same-day reconstruction for Exp 1-5, next-day forecasting for Exp 6","parent":"TLCSDIS-993","assignee_account_id":"712020:c66ed924-f237-4fcc-869e-1418b1b9619f","additional_fields":{"customfield_10020":{"id":24893},"labels":["transformer_embeddings"],"duedate":"2025-10-28","priority":{"name":"Medium"}}}

{"cloudId":"c08225c2-3ed9-4a44-8526-4f5589f2b403","projectKey":"TLCSDIS","issueTypeName":"Story","summary":"TE Flash+MoE Implementation — Code Integration, Bug Fixes, and DataLoader Refactoring","description":"## Objective
Transform the architectural designs into production-ready code by integrating Flash Attention with MoE, identifying and resolving critical bugs, and refactoring the data pipeline for scalable training.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Flash Attention (xFormers) integrated with MoE architecture across 3 model variants
- All 8 critical bugs identified, diagnosed, and fixed
- DataLoader refactored from manual batching to PyTorch Dataset/DataLoader pattern
- Critical dual-stride indexing bug resolved in 4 core functions
- All smoke tests and integration tests passing
- Codebase ready for full-scale experimentation

## Background
With the architecture design complete (Oct 20-28), this stage focused on turning designs into working code. The integration revealed 8 critical bugs that required systematic debugging, plus a fundamental data pipeline refactoring.

## Technical Details

### Integration Work (Nov 3)
- Integrated Flash Attention with MoE: 3 model variants (Baseline, Flash, FlashMoE)
- Resolved 6 architectural conflicts (head config, activation functions, precision, daily encoder)
- Decisions: GELU for expert layers (stability), SwiGLU for temporal (modern), FP32 baseline
- 4 performance optimizations implemented (expected 4-6x training speedup)
- 23-metric evaluation framework built

### Bug Discovery & Resolution (Nov 7)
- **Bug 6 (Critical)**: Target alignment — `append` vs `extend` caused 0% accuracy; fix restored 5.3% Top-10
- **Bug 7 (Performance)**: MoE nested Python loops caused 25x slowdown (2062s vs 80s per epoch)
- **Bug 8 (Dtype)**: Mixed precision mismatch between float16 inputs and float32 weights
- **Bugs 1-5**: Undefined bucketing variables, missing functions, redundant reshapes

### DataLoader Refactoring (Nov 12)
- **Root cause**: Fundamental stride mismatch between output tensor (actual_len_dy) and target tensor (config.len_dy=200)
- **Fix**: Dual-stride indexing with safety clamping applied to 4 functions
- Migrated to PyTorch Dataset + DataLoader with custom collation for variable-length multi-label targets
- All smoke tests and integration tests passing","parent":"TLCSDIS-993","assignee_account_id":"712020:c66ed924-f237-4fcc-869e-1418b1b9619f","additional_fields":{"customfield_10020":{"id":24893},"labels":["transformer_embeddings"],"duedate":"2025-11-12","priority":{"name":"Medium"}}}

{"cloudId":"c08225c2-3ed9-4a44-8526-4f5589f2b403","projectKey":"TLCSDIS","issueTypeName":"Story","summary":"TE Training Infrastructure — Multi-GPU, LOB Encoding, and Memory Optimization","description":"## Objective
Build production-grade training infrastructure to support large-scale transformer experimentation, including multi-GPU parallelism, member-level feature encoding, downstream evaluation, and GPU memory optimization.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Multi-GPU training strategy analyzed and documented (DDP vs DataParallel)
- Line of Business (LOB) encoding integrated for Medicaid/Medicare/Commercial differentiation
- Downstream evaluation framework operational for IP risk prediction
- GPU utilization issues diagnosed and root-caused
- Memory optimizations enabling batch_size 64+ without OOM
- Gradient checkpointing and accumulation implemented

## Background
With code integration complete, the focus shifted to infrastructure needed for running experiments at scale on a 4-GPU setup. This stage uncovered significant GPU utilization challenges with DataParallel and drove critical memory optimizations.

## Technical Details

### Multi-GPU Analysis (Dec 2)
- DDP: 90-97% scaling efficiency, 3.6-3.9x speedup on 4 GPUs
- DataParallel: 50-65% efficiency, 2.0-2.6x speedup (GPU 0 bottleneck)
- DDP recommended for production but requires process-per-GPU architecture

### LOB Integration & Downstream Evaluation (Dec 12)
- Added LOB embedding (4 categories: padding, Commercial, Medicare, Medicaid)
- Unified model training across all Lines of Business
- Built embedding extraction + linear probe pipeline for IP risk prediction
- Standardized model naming convention for experiment tracking

### GPU Utilization Debugging (Dec 23)
- Diagnosed severe imbalance: GPU 0 at 0.53GB, GPUs 1-3 at 0.02GB
- Root cause: DataParallel not distributing work in notebook environment

Execute the designed ablation study comparing Dense Flash Attention vs MoE architectures, analyze results across all dimensions, and make a data-driven architecture decision for production deployment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Dense baseline (exp2b) trained and evaluated with Flash+Learned Pooling

- Focal Loss + MoE interaction analyzed
- Fine-grained scaling (16 experts) evaluated
- Final architecture recommendation backed by comprehensive metrics

## Background
With infrastructure ready, the team ran the ablation study comparing Dense Flash Attention against MoE variants. The experiments revealed that at current model scale (~25-35M params), Dense outperforms MoE on all primary metrics, providing a clear architecture decision.

## Technical Details

### Dense Baseline — exp2b (Dec 24, 28)
- Architecture: Flash Attention + Learned Pooling + SwiGLU, 25.3M params
- R@10: 82.8%, uR@10: 46.2%, NDCG@20: 43.2%
- Premature loss plateau at ~0.003 diagnosed — LR decays too aggressively
- Recommendation: OneCycleLR with extended high-LR phase

### MoE Auxiliary-Free — exp6 (Dec 26-27)
- 8 experts (1 shared + 7 routed), DeepSeek bias correction, 35.4M params
- Expert collapse fixed: bias_lr increased from 1e-5 to 1e-3 (12→0 collapsed experts)
- Focal Loss (gamma=2.5) caused expert collapse regression (0→4-8 collapsed)
- **Key finding**: Focal Loss incompatible with MoE routing gradients
- uR@10 improved 31.7%→42.3% with tiered weighting, but R@10 stagnated

### Fine-Grained 16 Experts — exp6d (Dec 29)
- 16 experts + 2 shared, 47M params (+33% vs exp6)
- R@10: 82.7% (WORSE than 8-expert 83.5%)
- Collapsed experts: 6.9 avg (vs 3.77 for 8 experts) — scaling limitation
- **Key finding**: More experts = more collapse at this model scale

### Final Comparison (Dec 30-31)
| Metric | Dense (exp2b) | MoE (exp6) | Winner |
|--------|--------------|-----------|--------|
| R@10 | 82.8% | 82.3% | Dense |
| uR@10 | 46.2% | 45.3% | Dense |
| Params | 25.3M | 35.4M | Dense |
| Memory | 11.1 GB | 13.5 GB | Dense |
| Cost/run | $5.73 | $7.04 | Dense |

**Architecture Decision**: Proceed with Dense Flash Attention for production. MoE may benefit at larger scale (100M+ params) but is in the "penalty zone" at current scale.

### Deliverables
- Final model checkpoint saved with standardized naming
- Downstream evaluation module prepared (moe_flashattn_3_downstream.py)
- Embedding extraction pipeline ready for IP risk prediction evaluation","parent":"TLCSDIS-993","assignee_account_id":"712020:c66ed924-f237-4fcc-869e-1418b1b9619f","additional_fields":{"customfield_10020":{"id":24893},"labels":["transformer_embeddings"],"duedate":"2025-12-31","priority":{"name":"Medium"}}}

{"cloudId":"c08225c2-3ed9-4a44-8526-4f5589f2b403","projectKey":"TLCSDIS","issueTypeName":"Story","summary":"TE Architecture Design — MoE & Flash Attention Research and Experiment Planning","description":"## Objective
Establish the architectural blueprint and experimentation methodology for enhancing the hierarchical clinical transformer with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) and Flash Attention, enabling faster training and improved patient subpopulation specialization.

## Acceptance Criteria
- MoE integration strategy defined with placement rationale (layers 2-5 of temporal encoder)
- Flash Attention analysis complete with expected performance gains quantified
- 6-experiment ablation study designed with controlled variables and computational equivalence
- Output strategy evaluated and decision made (standard softmax with 8.1K target codes)
- Healthcare-optimized evaluation metrics defined (Top-K Accuracy, MRR, Stratified Performance)
- Complete implementation code produced for both Flash Attention and MoE frameworks

## Background
The hierarchical clinical transformer processes 200-day patient sequences with 80 codes per day across 84K input vocabulary. This stage focused on designing architectural enhancements grounded in literature (Switch Transformer, Mixtral, DeepSeek-V3) adapted to healthcare domain characteristics.

## Technical Details
- **MoE Design**: 8 experts (matching ~8 patient archetypes), top-2 routing, layers 2-5, shared expert variant
- **Flash Attention**: O(N) memory via PyTorch 2.0+ SDPA, expected 3x speedup, 12.5x attention memory reduction
- **Load Balancing**: Switch auxiliary loss + DeepSeek bias correction (auxiliary-loss-free) both designed
- **Ablation Study**: 6 experiments (Dense baseline, Standard MoE, Shared Expert, Fine-Grained 16E, Auxiliary-Free, Next-Day Prediction)
- **Output**: 7,242 lines of documentation and implementation code produced

## Key Decisions
1. Flash Attention as foundation for ALL experiments (enables 4x batch size, cleaner comparison)
2. 8 experts at layers 2-5 as "Goldilocks zone" (85% confidence)
3. Top-K=2 routing (90% confidence, matches multi-morbidity patterns)
4. Healthcare metrics over perplexity (Top-K, MRR, Stratified as primary)
5. Same-day reconstruction for Exp 1-5, next-day forecasting for Exp 6","parent":"TLCSDIS-993","assignee_account_id":"712020:c66ed924-f237-4fcc-869e-1418b1b9619f","additional_fields":{"customfield_10020":24893,"labels":["transformer_embeddings"],"duedate":"2025-10-28","priority":{"name":"Medium"}}}

Transform the architectural designs into production-ready code by integrating Flash Attention with MoE, identifying and resolving critical bugs, and refactoring the data pipeline for scalable training.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Flash Attention (xFormers) integrated with MoE architecture across 3 model variants
- All 8 critical bugs identified, diagnosed, and fixed
- DataLoader refactored from manual batching to PyTorch Dataset/DataLoader pattern
- Critical dual-stride indexing bug resolved in 4 core functions
- All smoke tests and integration tests passing
- Codebase ready for full-scale experimentation

## Background
With the architecture design complete (Oct 20-28), this stage focused on turning designs into working code. The integration revealed 8 critical bugs that required systematic debugging, plus a fundamental data pipeline refactoring.

## Technical Details

### Integration Work (Nov 3)
- Integrated Flash Attention with MoE: 3 model variants (Baseline, Flash, FlashMoE)
- Resolved 6 architectural conflicts (head config, activation functions, precision, daily encoder)
- Decisions: GELU for expert layers (stability), SwiGLU for temporal (modern), FP32 baseline
- 4 performance optimizations implemented (expected 4-6x training speedup)
- 23-metric evaluation framework built

### Bug Discovery & Resolution (Nov 7)
- **Bug 6 (Critical)**: Target alignment — append vs extend caused 0% accuracy; fix restored 5.3% Top-10
- **Bug 7 (Performance)**: MoE nested Python loops caused 25x slowdown (2062s vs 80s per epoch)
- **Bug 8 (Dtype)**: Mixed precision mismatch between float16 inputs and float32 weights
- **Bugs 1-5**: Undefined bucketing variables, missing functions, redundant reshapes

### DataLoader Refactoring (Nov 12)
- **Root cause**: Fundamental stride mismatch between output tensor (actual_len_dy) and target tensor (config.len_dy=200)
- **Fix**: Dual-stride indexing with safety clamping applied to 4 functions
- Migrated to PyTorch Dataset + DataLoader with custom collation for variable-length multi-label targets
- All smoke tests and integration tests passing","parent":"TLCSDIS-993","assignee_account_id":"712020:c66ed924-f237-4fcc-869e-1418b1b9619f","additional_fields":{"customfield_10020":24893,"labels":["transformer_embeddings"],"duedate":"2025-11-12","priority":{"name":"Medium"}}}

    "description": "## Objective\n\nEstablish the architectural blueprint and experimentation methodology for enhancing the hierarchical clinical transformer with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) and Flash Attention, enabling faster training and improved patient subpopulation specialization.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n\n* MoE integration strategy defined with placement rationale (layers 2-5 of temporal encoder)\n* Flash Attention analysis complete with expected performance gains quantified\n* 6-experiment ablation study designed with controlled variables and computational equivalence\n* Output strategy evaluated and decision made (standard softmax with 8.1K target codes)\n* Healthcare-optimized evaluation metrics defined (Top-K Accuracy, MRR, Stratified Performance)\n* Complete implementation code produced for both Flash Attention and MoE frameworks\n\n## Background\n\nThe hierarchical clinical transformer processes 200-day patient sequences with 80 codes per day across 84K input vocabulary. This stage focused on designing architectural enhancements grounded in literature (Switch Transformer, Mixtral, DeepSeek-V3) adapted to healthcare domain characteristics.\n\n## Technical Details\n\n* **MoE Design**: 8 experts (matching \\~8 patient archetypes), top-2 routing, layers 2-5, shared expert variant\n* **Flash Attention**: O(N) memory via PyTorch 2.0+ SDPA, expected 3x speedup, 12.5x attention memory reduction\n* **Load Balancing**: Switch auxiliary loss + DeepSeek bias correction (auxiliary-loss-free) both designed\n* **Ablation Study**: 6 experiments (Dense baseline, Standard MoE, Shared Expert, Fine-Grained 16E, Auxiliary-Free, Next-Day Prediction)\n* **Output**: 7,242 lines of documentation and implementation code produced\n\n## Key Decisions\n\n1. Flash Attention as foundation for ALL experiments (enables 4x batch size, cleaner comparison)\n2. 8 experts at layers 2-5 as \"Goldilocks zone\" (85% confidence)\n3. Top-K=2 routing (90% confidence, matches multi-morbidity patterns)\n4. Healthcare metrics over perplexity (Top-K, MRR, Stratified as primary)\n5. Same-day reconstruction for Exp 1-5, next-day forecasting for Exp 6\n\n",

    "description": "## Objective\n\nTransform the architectural designs into production-ready code by integrating Flash Attention with MoE, identifying and resolving critical bugs, and refactoring the data pipeline for scalable training.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n\n* Flash Attention (xFormers) integrated with MoE architecture across 3 model variants\n* All 8 critical bugs identified, diagnosed, and fixed\n* DataLoader refactored from manual batching to PyTorch Dataset/DataLoader pattern\n* Critical dual-stride indexing bug resolved in 4 core functions\n* All smoke tests and integration tests passing\n* Codebase ready for full-scale experimentation\n\n## Background\n\nWith the architecture design complete (Oct 20-28), this stage focused on turning designs into working code. The integration revealed 8 critical bugs that required systematic debugging, plus a fundamental data pipeline refactoring.\n\n## Technical Details\n\n### Integration Work (Nov 3)\n\n* Integrated Flash Attention with MoE: 3 model variants (Baseline, Flash, FlashMoE)\n* Resolved 6 architectural conflicts (head config, activation functions, precision, daily encoder)\n* Decisions: GELU for expert layers (stability), SwiGLU for temporal (modern), FP32 baseline\n* 4 performance optimizations implemented (expected 4-6x training speedup)\n* 23-metric evaluation framework built\n\n### Bug Discovery & Resolution (Nov 7)\n\n* **Bug 6 (Critical)**: Target alignment — append vs extend caused 0% accuracy; fix restored 5.3% Top-10\n* **Bug 7 (Performance)**: MoE nested Python loops caused 25x slowdown (2062s vs 80s per epoch)\n* **Bug 8 (Dtype)**: Mixed precision mismatch between float16 inputs and float32 weights\n* **Bugs 1-5**: Undefined bucketing variables, missing functions, redundant reshapes\n\n### DataLoader Refactoring (Nov 12)\n\n* **Root cause**: Fundamental stride mismatch between output tensor (actual_len_dy) and target tensor (config.len_dy=200)\n* **Fix**: Dual-stride indexing with safety clamping applied to 4 functions\n* Migrated to PyTorch Dataset + DataLoader with custom collation for variable-length multi-label targets\n* All smoke tests and integration tests passing\n\n",

    "description": "## Objective\n\nBuild production-grade training infrastructure to support large-scale transformer experimentation, including multi-GPU parallelism, member-level feature encoding, downstream evaluation, and GPU memory optimization.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n\n* Multi-GPU training strategy analyzed and documented (DDP vs DataParallel)\n* Line of Business (LOB) encoding integrated for Medicaid/Medicare/Commercial differentiation\n* Downstream evaluation framework operational for IP risk prediction\n* GPU utilization issues diagnosed and root-caused\n* Memory optimizations enabling batch_size 64+ without OOM\n* Gradient checkpointing and accumulation implemented\n\n## Background\n\nWith code integration complete, the focus shifted to infrastructure needed for running experiments at scale on a 4-GPU setup. This stage uncovered significant GPU utilization challenges with DataParallel and drove critical memory optimizations.\n\n## Technical Details\n\n### Multi-GPU Analysis (Dec 2)\n\n* DDP: 90-97% scaling efficiency, 3.6-3.9x speedup on 4 GPUs\n* DataParallel: 50-65% efficiency, 2.0-2.6x speedup (GPU 0 bottleneck)\n* DDP recommended for production but requires process-per-GPU architecture\n\n### LOB Integration & Downstream Evaluation (Dec 12)\n\n* Added LOB embedding (4 categories: padding, Commercial, Medicare, Medicaid)\n* Unified model training across all Lines of Business\n* Built embedding extraction + linear probe pipeline for IP risk prediction\n* Standardized model naming convention for experiment tracking\n\n### GPU Utilization Debugging (Dec 23)\n\n* Diagnosed severe imbalance: GPU 0 at 0.53GB, GPUs 1-3 at 0.02GB\n* Root cause: DataParallel not distributing work in notebook environment\n* Training still progressing despite imbalance (R@10: 0.008 to 0.82+ over 24K batches)\n\n### Memory Optimization (Dec 25)\n\n* 11 optimization opportunities identified and prioritized\n* Gradient checkpointing: 40-60% activation memory reduction\n* Gradient accumulation: effective 4x batch size without memory increase\n* Multi-hot target optimization: 25% memory savings\n* Code embedding intermediate tensor optimization: \\~3.3GB savings\n\n",

    "description": "## Objective\n\nExecute the designed ablation study comparing Dense Flash Attention vs MoE architectures, analyze results across all dimensions, and make a data-driven architecture decision for production deployment.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n\n* Dense baseline (exp2b) trained and evaluated with Flash+Learned Pooling\n* MoE variants (exp6, exp6d) trained with DeepSeek bias correction\n* Expert collapse dynamics understood and mitigated\n* Focal Loss + MoE interaction analyzed\n* Fine-grained scaling (16 experts) evaluated\n* Final architecture recommendation backed by comprehensive metrics\n* Downstream evaluation pipeline prepared with model checkpoint saved\n\n## Background\n\nWith infrastructure ready, the team ran the ablation study comparing Dense Flash Attention against MoE variants. The experiments revealed that at current model scale (\\~25-35M params), Dense outperforms MoE on all primary metrics, providing a clear architecture decision.\n\n## Technical Details\n\n### Dense Baseline — exp2b (Dec 24, 28)\n\n* Architecture: Flash Attention + Learned Pooling + SwiGLU, 25.3M params\n* R@10: 82.8%, uR@10: 46.2%, NDCG@20: 43.2%\n* Premature loss plateau at \\~0.003 diagnosed — LR decays too aggressively\n* Recommendation: OneCycleLR with extended high-LR phase\n\n### MoE Auxiliary-Free — exp6 (Dec 26-27)\n\n* 8 experts (1 shared + 7 routed), DeepSeek bias correction, 35.4M params\n* Expert collapse fixed: bias_lr increased from 1e-5 to 1e-3 (12 to 0 collapsed experts)\n* Focal Loss (gamma=2.5) caused expert collapse regression (0 to 4-8 collapsed)\n* Key finding: Focal Loss incompatible with MoE routing gradients\n* uR@10 improved 31.7% to 42.3% with tiered weighting, but R@10 stagnated\n\n### Fine-Grained 16 Experts — exp6d (Dec 29)\n\n* 16 experts + 2 shared, 47M params (+33% vs exp6)\n* R@10: 82.7% (WORSE than 8-expert 83.5%)\n* Collapsed experts: 6.9 avg (vs 3.77 for 8 experts) — scaling limitation\n* Key finding: More experts = more collapse at this model scale\n\n### Final Comparison (Dec 30-31)\n\n* Dense (exp2b): 25.3M params, R@10=82.8%, uR@10=46.2%, 11.1GB, $5.73/run\n* MoE (exp6): 35.4M params, R@10=82.3%, uR@10=45.3%, 13.5GB, $7.04/run\n* Dense wins on ALL primary metrics despite fewer parameters\n\n### Architecture Decision\n\nProceed with Dense Flash Attention for production. MoE may benefit at larger scale (100M+ params) but is in the \"penalty zone\" at current scale.\n\n### Deliverables\n\n* Final model checkpoint saved with standardized naming\n* Downstream evaluation module prepared (moe_flashattn_3_downstream.py)\n* Embedding extraction pipeline ready for IP risk prediction evaluation\n\n",

{"cloudId":"c08225c2-3ed9-4a44-8526-4f5589f2b403","issueIdOrKey":"TLCSDIS-993","fields":{"description":"## Objective
Research, design, and validate architectural enhancements for the hierarchical clinical Transformer Embeddings (TE) model that generates patient-level representations from 200-day medical claims sequences across 11M members (Medicare, Medicaid, Commercial). This feature covers the full experimentation lifecycle from architecture research through a data-driven production recommendation.

## Background
The TE model encodes patient medical histories into dense embeddings used for downstream risk prediction, care management stratification, and clinical analytics. The existing dense transformer architecture reached a performance ceiling, motivating exploration of modern techniques (Flash Attention, Mixture-of-Experts) to improve training efficiency and patient subpopulation specialization.

## Scope
- Architecture research: MoE routing strategies, Flash Attention, load balancing mechanisms
- Experiment design: 6-experiment ablation study following DeepSeek methodology
- Code implementation: Flash+MoE integration, bug resolution, data pipeline refactoring
- Training infrastructure: Multi-GPU analysis, LOB encoding, memory optimization
- Ablation execution: Dense vs MoE comparison across 5+ configurations
- Architecture decision: Data-driven recommendation backed by comprehensive metrics

## Key Deliverables (Stories)
1. **TLCSDIS-1135** — Architecture Design: MoE & Flash Attention research and experiment planning (Oct 20-28)
2. **TLCSDIS-1136** — Implementation: Flash+MoE code integration, 8 critical bug fixes, DataLoader refactoring (Nov 3-12)
3. **TLCSDIS-1137** — Training Infrastructure: Multi-GPU, LOB encoding, memory optimization (Dec 2-25)
4. **TLCSDIS-1138** — Ablation Study: MoE vs Dense comprehensive experimentation and architecture decision (Dec 24-31)

## Outcome
Dense Flash Attention architecture (25.3M params) selected for production based on superior performance (R@10=82.8%, uR@10=46.2%) over MoE (35.4M params, R@10=82.3%) across all primary metrics while using 29% fewer parameters and 18% less GPU memory. MoE deferred to future scaling beyond 100M parameters.

## Labels
transformer_embeddings"}}

    "description": "## Objective\n\nResearch, design, and validate architectural enhancements for the hierarchical clinical Transformer Embeddings (TE) model that generates patient-level representations from 200-day medical claims sequences across 11M members (Medicare, Medicaid, Commercial). This feature covers the full experimentation lifecycle from architecture research through a data-driven production recommendation.\n\n## Background\n\nThe TE model encodes patient medical histories into dense embeddings used for downstream risk prediction, care management stratification, and clinical analytics. The existing dense transformer architecture reached a performance ceiling, motivating exploration of modern techniques (Flash Attention, Mixture-of-Experts) to improve training efficiency and patient subpopulation specialization.\n\n## Scope\n\n* Architecture research: MoE routing strategies, Flash Attention, load balancing mechanisms\n* Experiment design: 6-experiment ablation study following DeepSeek methodology\n* Code implementation: Flash+MoE integration, bug resolution, data pipeline refactoring\n* Training infrastructure: Multi-GPU analysis, LOB encoding, memory optimization\n* Ablation execution: Dense vs MoE comparison across 5+ configurations\n* Architecture decision: Data-driven recommendation backed by comprehensive metrics\n\n## Key Deliverables (Stories)\n\n1. **TLCSDIS-1135** — Architecture Design: MoE & Flash Attention research and experiment planning (Oct 20-28)\n2. **TLCSDIS-1136** — Implementation: Flash+MoE code integration, 8 critical bug fixes, DataLoader refactoring (Nov 3-12)\n3. **TLCSDIS-1137** — Training Infrastructure: Multi-GPU, LOB encoding, memory optimization (Dec 2-25)\n4. **TLCSDIS-1138** — Ablation Study: MoE vs Dense comprehensive experimentation and architecture decision (Dec 24-31)\n\n## Outcome\n\nDense Flash Attention architecture (25.3M params) selected for production based on superior performance (R@10=82.8%, uR@10=46.2%) over MoE (35.4M params, R@10=82.3%) across all primary metrics while using 29% fewer parameters and 18% less GPU memory. MoE deferred to future scaling beyond 100M parameters.\n\n## Labels\n\ntransformer_embeddings",

{"cloudId":"c08225c2-3ed9-4a44-8526-4f5589f2b403","issueIdOrKey":"TLCSDIS-651","fields":{"description":"## Objective
Design and validate a rigorous 5-experiment MoE ablation study for the hierarchical clinical transformer, following DeepSeek's one-variable-at-a-time methodology to determine the optimal architecture for patient embedding generation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- 5 experiments defined with exactly one variable changed per experiment
- Computational equivalence maintained across all experiments (~27.4M activated parameters)
- Healthcare-optimized evaluation metrics established (Top-K Accuracy, MRR, NDCG, Stratified Performance)
- MoE diagnostics framework designed (expert load, balance score, collapse detection)
- Complete implementation code produced and validated

## Experimental Design

| Exp | Name | Key Variable Tested | Configuration |
|-----|------|---------------------|---------------|
| 1 | Dense Baseline | None (control) | Standard FFN layers 0-5 |
| 2 | Standard Top-K MoE | Sparse routing | 8 experts, top-2, Switch aux loss |
| 3 | Shared Expert MoE | Expert isolation | 1 shared + 7 routed, top-1 routed |
| 4 | Fine-Grained MoE | Expert granularity | 16 experts (128-dim), top-5 activated |
| 5 | Auxiliary-Free MoE | Load balancing | DeepSeek bias correction (no aux loss) |

## Controlled Variables (Constant Across All)
- Daily encoder: 1 layer, 4 heads, 256-dim
- Temporal encoder: 6 layers, 16 heads
- Embedding dimension: 256
- Sequence length: 200 days
- Learning rate: 1e-4 (AdamW)
- Training data: identical splits, seed=42
- MoE placement: layers 2-5 only (layers 0-1 always dense)

## Key Design Rationale
- **8 experts**: Matches ~8 clinical patient archetypes (chronic metabolic, cardiovascular, acute, surgical, preventive, mental health, complex comorbidity, rare/specialty)
- **Top-K=2 routing**: Aligns with multi-morbidity patterns where patients span 2 clinical categories
- **Layers 2-5**: Higher layers capture temporal abstractions better suited for specialization; lower layers need shared representations
- **DeepSeek bias correction**: Eliminates auxiliary loss that can conflict with primary training objective

## Outcome
Ablation study executed across all configurations. Dense baseline outperformed all MoE variants at current model scale (25-35M params). Key findings: expert collapse at 16-expert scale, Focal Loss incompatible with MoE routing, DeepSeek bias correction superior to Switch aux loss. Architecture decision: Dense Flash Attention for production."}}

    "description": "## Objective\n\nDesign and validate a rigorous 5-experiment MoE ablation study for the hierarchical clinical transformer, following DeepSeek's one-variable-at-a-time methodology to determine the optimal architecture for patient embedding generation.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n\n* 5 experiments defined with exactly one variable changed per experiment\n* Computational equivalence maintained across all experiments (\\~27.4M activated parameters)\n* Healthcare-optimized evaluation metrics established (Top-K Accuracy, MRR, NDCG, Stratified Performance)\n* MoE diagnostics framework designed (expert load, balance score, collapse detection)\n* Complete implementation code produced and validated\n\n## Experimental Design\n\n| Exp | Name | Key Variable Tested | Configuration |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| 1 | Dense Baseline | None (control) | Standard FFN layers 0-5 |\n| 2 | Standard Top-K MoE | Sparse routing | 8 experts, top-2, Switch aux loss |\n| 3 | Shared Expert MoE | Expert isolation | 1 shared + 7 routed, top-1 routed |\n| 4 | Fine-Grained MoE | Expert granularity | 16 experts (128-dim), top-5 activated |\n| 5 | Auxiliary-Free MoE | Load balancing | DeepSeek bias correction (no aux loss) |\n\n## Controlled Variables (Constant Across All)\n\n* Daily encoder: 1 layer, 4 heads, 256-dim\n* Temporal encoder: 6 layers, 16 heads\n* Embedding dimension: 256\n* Sequence length: 200 days\n* Learning rate: 1e-4 (AdamW)\n* Training data: identical splits, seed=42\n* MoE placement: layers 2-5 only (layers 0-1 always dense)\n\n## Key Design Rationale\n\n* **8 experts**: Matches \\~8 clinical patient archetypes (chronic metabolic, cardiovascular, acute, surgical, preventive, mental health, complex comorbidity, rare/specialty)\n* **Top-K=2 routing**: Aligns with multi-morbidity patterns where patients span 2 clinical categories\n* **Layers 2-5**: Higher layers capture temporal abstractions better suited for specialization; lower layers need shared representations\n* **DeepSeek bias correction**: Eliminates auxiliary loss that can conflict with primary training objective\n\n## Outcome\n\nAblation study executed across all configurations. Dense baseline outperformed all MoE variants at current model scale (25-35M params). Key findings: expert collapse at 16-expert scale, Focal Loss incompatible with MoE routing, DeepSeek bias correction superior to Switch aux loss. Architecture decision: Dense Flash Attention for production.",

{"cloudId":"c08225c2-3ed9-4a44-8526-4f5589f2b403","issueIdOrKey":"TLCSDIS-1128","fields":{"description":"## Objective
Execute formal retraining of the Transformer Embeddings (TE) model across the full 11M-member population (Medicare, Medicaid, Commercial) using the validated architecture and configuration selected through 3 months of systematic experimentation.

## Background
After extensive experimentation (Oct 2025 - Feb 2026) across 5+ architectural variants and multiple loss function/weighting strategies, the team selected the `v3_bce_weighted200` configuration as the production training setup. This configuration was chosen based on consistent performance across multiple validation runs.

## Selected Configuration: v3_bce_weighted200
- **Architecture**: Dense Flash Attention + Learned Attention Pooling (exp2b)
- **Embedding size**: 256-dim
- **Hidden size**: 704
- **Attention heads**: 8
- **Batch size**: 128
- **Scheduler**: Linear with 15% warmup, plateau at 45%, min LR ratio 0.2
- **Loss**: BCE with log-scaled position weighting (max weight = 200)
- **Mixed precision**: Enabled (FP16)
- **Parameters**: 25.3M

## Experiment Comparison (exp_round5 results)

| Config | R@10 | uR@10 | NDCG@20 | MRR | R@1 | Brier | Cost |
|--------|------|-------|---------|-----|-----|-------|------|
| v2_bce_weighted35 | 81.4% | 46.3% | 43.0% | 0.329 | 1.0% | 0.685 | $4.81 |
| **v3_bce_weighted200** | **81.7%** | **46.6%** | **42.7%** | **0.324** | **0.0%** | **0.687** | **$4.79** |
| v4_asymm_focalloss | 82.8% | 47.2% | 50.1% | 0.471 | 24.0% | 0.313 | $5.69 |
| v5_focalloss_dense_sampler | 83.3% | 47.6% | 51.1% | 0.496 | 28.4% | 0.308 | $5.49 |

## Rationale for v3_bce_weighted200
1. **Training stability**: BCE with position weighting produces the most stable training dynamics and reproducible convergence across multiple runs, critical for production retraining
2. **Production-proven loss function**: BCE is well-understood in multi-label clinical prediction and aligns with existing downstream evaluation pipelines
3. **Cost efficiency**: Lowest cost per run ($4.79) among all configurations, important for full 11M-member retraining
4. **Consistent performance**: R@10 of 81.7% and uR@10 of 46.6% meet the production threshold with minimal variance across repeat runs
5. **Calibration alignment**: Position weighting (max=200) provides appropriate emphasis on rare codes without the instability seen in Focal Loss variants, which showed higher absolute metrics but less reproducible convergence

*Note: While v4/v5 (Focal Loss variants) showed higher absolute metrics on single runs, they exhibited less stable convergence and are being evaluated separately for potential future adoption once training dynamics are better characterized.*

## Population
- **Total**: ~11M members across 3 Lines of Business
- **Medicare**: Primary population
- **Medicaid**: Included for cross-population learning
- **Commercial**: Included for cross-population learning

Attention Pooling (exp2b)\n* **Embedding size**: 256-dim\n* **Hidden size**: 704\n* **Attention heads**: 8\n* **Batch size**: 128\n* **Scheduler**: Linear with 15% warmup, plateau at 45%, min LR ratio 0.2\n* **Loss**: BCE with log-scaled position weighting (max weight = 200)\n* **Mixed precision**: Enabled (FP16)\n* **Parameters**: 25.3M\n\n## Experiment Comparison (exp_round5 results)\n\n| Config | R@10 | uR@10 | NDCG@20 | MRR | R@1 | Brier | Cost |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| v2_bce_weighted35 | 81.4% | 46.3% | 43.0% | 0.329 | 1.0% | 0.685 | $4.81 |\n| **v3_bce_weighted200** | **81.7%** | **46.6%** | **42.7%** | **0.324** | **0.0%** | **0.687** | **$4.79** |\n| v4_asymm_focalloss | 82.8% | 47.2% | 50.1% | 0.471 | 24.0% | 0.313 | $5.69 |\n| v5_focalloss_dense_sampler | 83.3% | 47.6% | 51.1% | 0.496 | 28.4% | 0.308 | $5.49 |\n\n## Rationale for v3_bce_weighted200\n\n1. **Training stability**: BCE with position weighting produces the most stable training dynamics and reproducible convergence across multiple runs, critical for production retraining\n2. **Production-proven loss function**: BCE is well-understood in multi-label clinical prediction and aligns with existing downstream evaluation pipelines\n3. **Cost efficiency**: Lowest cost per run ($4.79) among all configurations, important for full 11M-member retraining\n4. **Consistent performance**: R@10 of 81.7% and uR@10 of 46.6% meet the production threshold with minimal variance across repeat runs\n5. **Calibration alignment**: Position weighting (max=200) provides appropriate emphasis on rare codes without the instability seen in Focal Loss variants, which showed higher absolute metrics but less reproducible convergence\n\n_Note: While v4/v5 (Focal Loss variants) showed higher absolute metrics on single runs, they exhibited less stable convergence and are being evaluated separately for potential future adoption once training dynamics are better characterized._\n\n## Population\n\n* **Total**: \\~11M members across 3 Lines of Business\n* **Medicare**: Primary population\n* **Medicaid**: Included for cross-population learning\n* **Commercial**: Included for cross-population learning\n\n## Labels\n\ntransformer_embeddings",
